_about: Pro variants for the three most repeated scenes: offseason training, summer break and holder chemistry.

scenarios.title: The Empty Facility
scenarios.text: The season is over and the facility is nearly empty: a few rehab players, the strength staff and a coffee machine nobody cleans. You have a few weeks to build something before camp.

choices.label: Build the leg
choices.result: Squats, sled pushes and long kicks into the wind, five mornings a week. Your leg aches by lunch, and by June the ball sounds different coming off your foot.

choices.label: Groove the stroke
choices.result: Five hundred kicks a week from the same three spots, every one charted on a clipboard. It's boring, and the stroke that comes out of it is boringly perfect.

choices.label: Train the head
choices.result: Breathing work, visualization and pressure games with the team psychologist, who makes you kick with a stadium's noise in your headphones. Your heart rate stops jumping by May.

choices.label: Rebuild the body
choices.result: Core, hips and the small muscles nobody films, with the strength staff three days a week. You come out of it moving like a younger player and sleeping like a stone.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Program
scenarios.text: The strength coach slides a printed offseason program across the desk: four tracks, each one highlighted in a different color, and a note at the bottom that says pick one and own it.

choices.label: Take the power track
choices.result: The power track, the yellow one: heavy lifts, sprints and kicks from a little farther back every week. It's brutal, and the extra yards show up by the end of spring.

choices.label: Take the precision track
choices.result: The green track, all precision: narrow posts, odd angles and a target taped to the net. The misses get smaller until they nearly stop, and the coach starts bringing friends to watch.

choices.label: Take the mental track
choices.result: The blue track, the strange one: meditation, sleep coaching and kicking with a buzzer that goes off at random. It's uncomfortable, and by camp nothing rattles you at all.

choices.label: Take the conditioning track
choices.result: The red track: running, mobility and hours in the pool with the linemen. You're the fittest specialist in the building by camp, and the linemen stop calling you 'the kicker'.

scenarios.title: The Garage Gym
scenarios.text: No facility this spring: the club is renovating, so it's your garage, a borrowed rack, a high school field down the road and whatever discipline you can find on your own at six in the morning.

choices.label: Lift in the garage
choices.result: The borrowed rack in the garage, every morning before the neighbors wake up. It's cold and loud and lonely, and your legs come out of it stronger than they've ever been.

choices.label: Kick at the high school
choices.result: The high school field, a bag of balls and the groundskeeper who lets you in early. You kick until the stroke is automatic, and the varsity kicker starts showing up to watch.

choices.label: Work on the quiet parts
choices.result: Journals, film on the laptop, long walks and a phone call a week with the sports psychologist. It doesn't look like training to the neighbors, and it changes how you handle pressure.

choices.label: Run the hills
choices.result: The steep road behind the house, run until your lungs burn, every second day. Your body hardens, and the neighbors start timing you from their porch.

scenarios.title: The Film Says
scenarios.text: The coaches send you home with a hard drive of last season's kicks and a short note: three things we'd like to see fixed by camp. You have a few weeks, and you can only really fix one.

choices.label: Fix the distance
choices.result: The long ones, first: a power program with a specialist and kicks from deeper every week. The coaches' note had distance at the top for a reason, and you treat it that way.

choices.label: Fix the misses
choices.result: The misses, one by one, sorted by direction and broken down frame by frame. Most of them start in your plant foot, and by camp your plant foot is a different animal.

choices.label: Fix the big moments
choices.result: The kicks that mattered most, watched again and again with the psychologist until they stop feeling dangerous. You come into camp with a calmer pulse and a quieter head.

choices.label: Fix the body first
choices.result: None of the three, at first: your body, which the film says is tired. Six weeks of conditioning later, the other problems start fixing themselves.

scenarios.title: A Kicker Tags Along
scenarios.text: A young kicker from another club asks to train with you this offseason. He's eager, a little loud, and willing to do whatever you're doing, every single morning, if you'll let him tag along.

choices.label: Lift together
choices.result: Heavy lifting together, three mornings a week, and he pushes you harder than any coach would. Neither of you wants to be the one who stops first, and both legs get stronger.

choices.label: Compete on the targets
choices.result: A target competition every day, loser buys breakfast. You buy breakfast a lot in April and almost never by June, and your stroke is the sharpest it's been.

choices.label: Teach him the head game
choices.result: You teach him the mental side, and teaching it makes you better at it. By the end of spring you both breathe the same way before every kick, and he calls it your trick.

choices.label: Train alone after all
choices.result: You thank him and train alone, with a conditioning plan and a lot of quiet. You come back healthier than you've been in years, and he finds another partner happily.

scenarios.title: The Long Spring
scenarios.text: A long spring with nothing on the calendar but camp in July. Your body has opinions about what it needs, and so do your agent, the coaches and the trainer who texts you every week.

choices.label: Listen to the coaches
choices.result: The coaches want distance, so you give them distance: a strength block, then long kicks on windy days. It's the hardest spring you've had, and the leg answers.

choices.label: Listen to your own notes
choices.result: Your own notes from last season say accuracy, so you chase it: narrow posts, bad angles and a lot of patience. The coaches notice the difference in the first week of camp.

choices.label: Listen to your agent
choices.result: Your agent says the market pays for calm, so you work on calm: the psychologist, the routines, the breath. It's quiet work, and it shows up in every pressure drill.

choices.label: Listen to the trainer
choices.result: The trainer says your body needs rebuilding, so you rebuild it: mobility, strength and a lot of sleep. You arrive at camp feeling better than you did as a rookie.

scenarios.title: A Few Free Weeks
scenarios.text: A few free weeks before camp, and for once nobody needs you anywhere. The phone has three invitations on it: a road trip, a youth camp and a course you've been meaning to take.

choices.label: Take the road trip
choices.result: A week on the road with {best_friend}, gas station snacks and bad music, sleeping wherever the night ends. You come home sunburned and lighter than you've felt all year.

choices.label: Coach at the youth camp
choices.result: A week at a youth camp in the hills, teaching ten-year-olds to kick. They think you're a superstar, and the one who finally makes a kick from twenty yards cries happy tears.

choices.label: Take the course
choices.result: A short course in something you've always wanted to understand, with homework and a professor who doesn't care about football. It's humbling, and you like the person it makes you.

scenarios.title: The Lake House
scenarios.text: {sibling} has rented a lake house for two weeks and wants the whole family there. There's a dock, a boat that barely starts, and a list of projects you are definitely being asked to help with.

choices.label: Go for the whole two weeks
choices.result: Two full weeks at the lake: the dock, the boat, the cousins and a lot of terrible card tricks. Nobody mentions football once, and you sleep better than you have in a year.

choices.label: Teach the cousins to kick
choices.result: You set up a goal with two oars and a rope and teach every cousin to kick. The tournament at the end of the week becomes a family legend, with handmade trophies.

choices.label: Go for a weekend and read
choices.result: One weekend at the lake, and the rest of the time at home with a stack of books you've been meaning to read. You come back to camp with a head full of ideas.

scenarios.title: The Empty City
scenarios.text: The city empties out in summer: the season's over, the crowds are gone, and the streets you only ever see on the way to the facility have street fairs and night markets on them.

choices.label: See the city properly
choices.result: Every night market, every street fair, every neighborhood you've only driven through. You meet more people in two weeks than in two seasons, and some of them become friends.

choices.label: Run a free clinic
choices.result: A free kicking clinic in a city park every Saturday, with the snapper helping. The crowds grow every week, and by the last one the local news shows up.

choices.label: Find a quiet project
choices.result: A quiet project: a language app, a cooking class, a garden on the balcony. It fills the long evenings, and it reminds you there's a person under the helmet.

scenarios.title: The Old Friends
scenarios.text: Your old friends from home have planned a week away and booked you in without asking. The group chat is already full of plans, packing lists and photos of a cabin with no internet.

choices.label: Go, no phone
choices.result: You go, and the phone stays in a drawer at the cabin. A week of old jokes, campfires and arguments about nothing, and you come home feeling young again.

choices.label: Go, and run the mornings
choices.result: You go, and you run the mornings: a hike, a swim, a kicking contest with a ball you brought. The old friends grumble and then demand a rematch every day.

choices.label: Send them off and stay home
choices.result: You send them off with your blessing and stay home to rest, read and sort out the house. The photos are great, and so is the quiet, and you don't regret it.

scenarios.title: The Charity Tour
scenarios.text: The players' union is running a summer tour of small towns: clinics, hospital visits and a softball game against the local firefighters. They need one more player for two weeks.

choices.label: Join the tour
choices.result: Two weeks in a bus with five teammates and a lot of small-town diners. The softball game is a disaster, the clinics are wonderful, and you come home with a bag of handmade gifts.

choices.label: Lead the clinics
choices.result: You take charge of the kicking clinics, town after town, and train two local coaches to run them after you leave. The union asks you to do it again next year.

choices.label: Help plan it from home
choices.result: You help plan the tour from home: the schedules, the hospitals, the sponsors. It's useful, invisible work, and it leaves you rested and a little wiser about how things get done.

scenarios.title: The Unplanned Summer
scenarios.text: For the first time in years, the summer has no plan at all. The house is quiet, the calendar is blank until camp, and {parent} keeps calling to ask what you're doing with yourself.

choices.label: Say yes to everything
choices.result: You say yes to every invitation that comes in: barbecues, weddings, a friend's band in a tiny bar. It's chaotic and wonderful, and you see people you'd almost lost touch with.

choices.label: Spend it with {parent}
choices.result: You spend a few weeks with {parent}, fixing things around the house and helping out in the neighborhood. The neighbors' kids follow you around asking for kicking tips.

choices.label: Learn something properly
choices.result: You pick one thing and learn it properly: a language, an instrument, a trade. It's slow and humbling, and by camp you can do something you couldn't do in May.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry: The New Spin
scenarios.text: {holder} has been fiddling with how they spin the laces, and the timing is a hair off in practice. They want to stay late this week and get it right, just the two of you and the jugs machine.

choices.label: Stay late every night
choices.result: Late every night, until the spin and your step line up again. By Thursday it's back, maybe better than before, and {holder} buys the pizza to celebrate.

choices.label: Ask them to switch back
choices.result: You ask {holder}, kindly, to go back to the old spin until the season's over. They agree after a long look, and you both know it's a conversation for the spring.

choices.label: Film it and compare
choices.result: Two angles of film, side by side, old spin and new spin, for an evening. You find the problem together on a laptop instead of on a cold field, and nobody's legs pay for it.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry: The Bad Week
scenarios.text: {holder} had a rough week: two bobbled holds in practice and a quiet bus ride home. They ask if you'll stay after on Wednesday, mostly, you suspect, so they don't have to be alone with it.

choices.label: Stay as long as they need
choices.result: As long as they need, and longer. You catch, hold and kick until the bobbles stop, and then you sit on the bench and talk about anything except football.

choices.label: Take them to dinner instead
choices.result: No practice at all: dinner at the place {holder} likes, and a long talk. The holds on Thursday are perfect, and neither of you mentions why.

choices.label: Bring in the snapper
choices.result: The snapper gets a call, and it becomes a unit session, with jokes and a competition. Spreading it across three people takes the weight off {holder}, which is what they needed.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry: The Weather
scenarios.text: The forecast for Sunday is wind, rain and a cold front, and {holder} wants to practice in the worst of it this week: wet balls, numb hands, and a hose the equipment staff have agreed to point at you.

choices.label: Practice in the hose
choices.result: Every snap, every hold, every kick under the hose, until your hands stop feeling the cold. It's miserable and funny, and by Friday nothing about wet weather surprises either of you.

choices.label: Save your legs for Sunday
choices.result: You save your legs for the weather and let {holder} work with the backup instead. They understand, mostly, and your leg is fresh on a day when it needs to be.

choices.label: Study wet-weather film
choices.result: Wet-weather film from every stadium you've played in, studied together over two evenings. You both learn exactly how a wet ball behaves, and you make a plan.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry: The Routine
scenarios.text: {holder} wants to rebuild your pre-kick routine from scratch: the count, the steps, the look, the nod. They've written it all out on an index card, and they're very proud of the index card.

choices.label: Try their routine
choices.result: You try their routine for a week, every rep, exactly as written. Half of it sticks and half of it doesn't, and the half that sticks is better than what you had.

choices.label: Keep your own
choices.result: You keep your own routine, thank them for the card, and pin it on your locker anyway. {holder} laughs and says the card was half a joke, and you're not sure which half.

choices.label: Build one together
choices.result: You build a new routine together over two late sessions, a little of yours and a little of theirs. It belongs to both of you now, which makes it stronger.

scenarios.title: Holder Chemistry: The Young Snapper
scenarios.text: There's a young snapper on the roster this week, filling in for an injury, and his snaps are fast and a little wild. {holder} wants the three of you to stay after every day until the timing settles.

choices.label: Stay with both of them
choices.result: Every day after practice, the three of you and a bag of balls. The young snapper settles by Thursday, and he thanks you both with a nervousness that's hard not to like.

choices.label: Let {holder} handle it
choices.result: You let {holder} handle the snapper and save your leg. They do it well, the timing settles by Friday, and {holder} enjoys being in charge for once.

choices.label: Give him your film
choices.result: You give the young snapper a folder of film and notes from the best snappers you've worked with. He studies it all night and shows up with questions you've never been asked.
